chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi narrated to me from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:
The affliction of the people is great: if we call them, they do not respond to us; and if we leave them, they will not be guided by anyone other than us.

key_terms.بغيرنا: Bi-ghayrina - by other than us; emphasizes the exclusive role of the Ahl al-Bayt in guidance
key_terms.بلية: Baliyya - affliction, trial, tribulation; here referring to the spiritual crisis of the community
key_terms.دعوناهم: Da'awnahum - we called/invited them; refers to the Imams' efforts to guide the community
key_terms.يهتدوا: Yahtadu - they find guidance; from the root h-d-y (guidance), a central Quranic concept

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the people and guidance through the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expresses the profound dilemma faced by the Ahl al-Bayt in guiding the Muslim community. Speaking in a gathering narrated through al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, the Imam laments that the people neither heed their call nor can find guidance elsewhere, highlighting the indispensable role of the Imams as the sole source of divine guidance after the Prophet. This reflects the Shia understanding that the Imams are the divinely appointed guides whose authority is essential for the community's spiritual welfare.
